title: A GPCR-Signaling Addiction Hub in the Murine Nucleus Accumbens and Its Partial Restitution by a GLP-1 Receptor Agonist: A Retrospective Transcriptomic Analysis
content: Substance use disorders, including opioid use disorder, cocaine use disorder, alcohol use disorder, and behavioral disorders including food addiction, represent immense global health and economic burdens. Although initiated by distinct pharmacological mechanisms, these conditions converge on shared reward and compulsive neural circuitry within the mesocorticolimbic system, particularly the nucleus accumbens (NAc). Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs), developed for metabolic indications, have recently demonstrated activity in suppressing craving across multiple substance classes. We tested the hypothesis that there exists a shared transcriptomic hub across OUD, CUD, AUD, and FA that is restituted by GLP-1 RA. We conducted a retrospective transcriptomic analysis of publicly available bulk RNA-seq data from the murine NAc across these addictions, alongside an addiction-naive GLP-1 RA treatment model. At the individual gene level, cross-addiction overlap was not observed. Submitting top-ranked transcripts per condition to gene list enrichment and functional annotation analyses revealed shared upregulation of G-protein coupled receptor (GPCR) signaling with GLP-1 RA administration exhibiting a discordant, restitutive transcriptional signature. These findings demonstrate that in the murine NAc, diverse addictive substances converge on NAc GPCR overactivation with restitution of signaling, at least, in part, by a GLP-1 RA.
